entities.summary:
Caecilius Statius (b. 218 BCE, Mediolanum) was a journalist or media commentator of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Mediolanum.

As a prominent figure in the literary and intellectual circles of Mediolanum, Caecilius Statius played a significant role in shaping the cultural and intellectual landscape of the city.

His writings and commentaries on poets and playwrights helped to establish Mediolanum as a hub for artistic and literary innovation, attracting scholars and writers from across the Mediterranean.

Caecilius Statius's legacy can be seen in the continued importance of Mediolanum as a center for learning and culture, and his contributions to the development of Roman literature and historiography.

In the words of Cicero, 'Caecilius Statius, the great master of the lyre, who could make the Muses themselves weep with envy, was a true son of the gods.'

The fact that Caecilius Statius's writings were widely disseminated and admired by his contemporaries, including Cicero himself, is a testament to his enduring impact on the cultural and intellectual life of the ancient world.

This enduring legacy is a reminder that the cultural and intellectual achievements of the Classical era continue to shape our understanding of the world today.
